title: Exercise: Push-On, Push-Off Toggle
oneLiner: One pushbutton turns a lamp on, the next press turns it off. Easy to describe, and a classic trap for code that acts on the level instead of the edge.
keyTakeaway: Toggle on the rising edge (an R_TRIG's Q, or Button AND NOT ButtonPrev), never on the button's level.
explanation:
One pushbutton that turns a light on with one press and off with the next. It sounds trivial, but a program that toggles whenever the button is TRUE flips the light once per scan for as long as the button is held, ending up on or off at random.

The fix is to act on the press, the rising edge, rather than on the level. The grader checks that each press changes the lamp exactly once, however long the button is held, and that even a one-scan tap counts.
